purpose: Controlled swap of the face embedder on frozen generated images.
interpretation: Cosine similarity between embeddings is not a probability and no calibrated identity threshold is used. Candidate pairings maximise total cosine similarity; weak matches are still assigned. Both arms see identical detections and identical 112x112 aligned crops.

controlled_variable.changed: recognition network weights and their input normalisation

detector.license: Pretrained weights: non-commercial research only; library code: MIT.

arcface.license: Pretrained weights: non-commercial research only; library code: MIT.
arcface.output: 512-d, L2-normalised here from the raw graph output

adaface.derived_from: Official AdaFace pretrained weights, exported to ONNX and hosted in the yakhyo/uniface-weights repository.

paper.title: AdaFace: Quality Adaptive Margin for Face Recognition

adaface.license: Research use only. The AdaFace project releases its code under the MIT licence and states that the pretrained models are for non-commercial research purposes; this record repeats that restriction rather than asserting any additional grant. Treat these weights like the buffalo_l weights: do not redistribute them or present their scores as a commercial identity system.
adaface.output: 512-d, unit length from the graph (ReduceL2 + Div); re-normalised here as a no-op check

preprocessing_validation.method: Same alignment and the same crops feed both arms; a candidate index is a position in a photo, not an identity label, so the across-pass comparison is a separation check, not ground truth.

comparison.scored_pairs_note: Only appearances that received a face under both arms; the October second pass drops a different character in each arm.

detection_control.method: One SCRFD detection pass per image feeds both arms, so per-image face counts cannot differ; only which expected character a row is paired with, or left without a face, can change.

baseline_check.note: The ArcFace arm reproduces the frozen baseline, so both arms share its detections, crops and pairing rule.

preprocessing_sweep.note: Two failure modes are visible here: an unscaled 0-255 input collapses every cosine towards 0.9, and a wrong channel order or scale lowers the same-index boost. The selected candidate is the AdaFace training convention (RGB, (x - 127.5) / 127.5), not the best-scoring row, because ranking normalisations against these few evaluation pairs would be tuning on the evaluation set.
